[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided a classic buttermilk scone recipe with the following ingredients:

[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1/2 teaspoon baking powder  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1/2 teaspoon salt  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1/2 cup (115g) cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3/4 cup (180ml) buttermilk  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1 large egg, beaten  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Optional: 1 teaspoon vanilla extract  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided detailed instructions for making the scones, including preheating the oven to 400°F (200°C) and baking for 15-20 minutes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested tips and variations for the scone recipe, including using cold butter, making a buttermilk substitute, adding lemon zest, and incorporating dried fruits.

[USER] The user asked if they can substitute all-purpose flour with bread flour.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Explained that bread flour can be used but will affect the final texture and character of the scones.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Noted that bread flour has a higher protein content, which can lead to a chewier, denser scone.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided tips for using bread flour, including reducing the buttermilk by 1-2 tablespoons and being gentle when mixing the dough.
